title: This Startup Is Trying to Bring Back Twitter
paragraphs: In October 2022, Elon Musk bought Twitter for $44 billion. At the time, Twitter was known for its short social media posts — called "tweets" — and its logo of a white bird on a light blue background.
Then, in April 2023, Twitter was renamed X, and its famous bird became a thing of the past.
But now, it may be coming back.
A startup called Operation Bluebird is "taking Twitter back," according to its website.
Twitter.now is not a copy of the old Twitter, but it does have the same light blue color and a white bird logo that's similar to the old Twitter logo.
Stephen Coates, who previously worked for Twitter, is one of the startup's founders. "Get over your X. The bird is back," he wrote on LinkedIn in August.
With Operation Bluebird, his team hopes to create a platform that lets users decide for themselves the types of posts they see, rather than having algorithms make those decisions for them.
The Operation Bluebird website describes old Twitter as "a place where the whole world came to talk" — and it wants to go back to that.
But how did Operation Bluebird get the right to use the name Twitter?
In December 2025, Operation Bluebird filed a petition with the US Patent and Trademark Office, saying that X had stopped using the trademarks "Twitter" and "tweet" after the name change.
Operation Bluebird also tried to get its own "Twitter" trademark.
Musk's X then sued the startup for copyright infringement — but a US judge tentatively agreed that X may have lost its rights to the Twitter trademark. The case is still open.
Right now, Twitter.now is still in its early stages, but people can pay $20 to become "founders" and be among the first to use it.
